title: More program, more adherence?
hook: Does a multi-part intervention guarantee a measurable improvement?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish intervention complexity from evidence of benefit in a randomized result.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish intervention complexity from evidence of benefit in a randomized result.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy program with four components has outcome ninety, matching control at ninety. What is the observed difference? Toy inputs A=[90, 90, 4]; B=[95, 90, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[0, 90, 4], [5, 95, 1]]. Labels: Difference, Program, Components.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Counting intervention components is not the same as measuring benefit. The comparison has fewer components and a larger supplied outcome difference. The toy makes that distinction; uncertainty and causal interpretation still depend on the study design.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Program outcome=95, Control outcome=90, Components=1. What is Difference? Answer: 5.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Program outcome=95, Control outcome=90, Components=1. What is Difference?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 5. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: A multi-part behavioral program for heart-attack patients' medication adherence had no effect (Volpp et al., 2017).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish intervention complexity from evidence of benefit in a randomized result.
